support: Each time I heard the smack of a ball against the boards, I pictured the throw that would one day split a box wide open.
The smaller colony from the eaves still feels light when I tip its box, and on windy nights I lie awake wondering whether it has stored enough honey to last until spring.
WV12-P02.5.note: The narrator pictures a ball splitting a box and lies awake over whether the light colony can survive the winter, which is worry rather than longing, criticism, amusement or admiration.

support: A century after it was built, the chimney stands as straight and sound as the day its last brick was laid, the best-made thing on the hill.
